blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet open-source models still struggle on long-horizon tasks, largely for lack of both training data and a working recipe, and scaling both is hard: long, complex tasks are difficult to curate and verify, and their rewards are sparse. We address both. First, we introduce Tev-Gym, the first long-horizon agent training dataset with verifiable, dense, progressive rewards -- 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains. It is built on a latent-world-first approach that first constructs a latent world: a complete and correct hidden specification of the task domain, workflow, and expected state after each step. Each task is then progressively rendered from this specification into an agent-facing environment, enabling controllable complexity and a natural progress metric. Second, we turn this metric into a training recipe: via progress-potential reward shaping (PPRS), we convert progress into a dense per-step reward that improves training efficiency and makes otherwise-intractable tasks trainable. Training with this recipe yields Tev-27B, which achieves substantial gains on the Agents' Last Exam computing and math sciences domains (ALE-CM), matching GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 at Pass@5. Despite training only on ALE-related data, it generalizes to the Terminal-Bench (TB) 3.0 and 4.0 subsets, surpassing GLM 5.2 and Gemini 3.7 Flash, and reaches Claude Opus 4.8-level performance on middle-horizon tasks such as TB 2.1.

Recent progress in large language models (LLMs) has shifted attention toward long-horizon
agents ( OpenAI, 2026 ; Anthropic, 2026 ; Moonshot AI, 2026 ) , which can work autonomously for hours to days on
complex, economically valuable tasks ( Sun et al., 2026 ; Styles et al., 2024 ; Zhu et al., 2026a ) .

blocks.en:
Despite these promising breakthroughs, coding-agent progress in the open-source community has focused on shorter- and
mid-horizon tasks, scaled via large agentic training corpora such as SWE-Smith ( Yang et al., 2025a ) ,
TMAX ( Ivison et al., 2026 ) , Endless Terminals ( Gandhi et al., 2026 ) , CLI-Gym ( Lin et al., 2026 ) ,
SETA ( Shen et al., 2026 ) , and Terminal-Universe ( Wu et al., 2026 ) . These datasets contain thousands to tens of thousands of environments, but each involves only a pull-request-sized fix or a short terminal session, and their unit-test-based evaluation provides only a terminal pass/fail signal or the fraction of tests passed. By contrast, genuinely long-horizon tasks are available only in human-authored benchmarks ( Merrill et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026b ) . These benchmarks contain only tens to a few hundred instances, each requiring weeks of expert effort. They provide partial credit only through hand-written checkpoints and exist only as evaluation sets. Thus, no training corpus of long-horizon tasks exists: agentic training corpora are large but short-horizon, while long-horizon tasks exist only as small, human-authored evaluation sets.

blocks.en:
Curating long-horizon tasks requires balancing two competing goals: tasks must be sufficiently long and structurally complex to provide meaningful training while remaining exactly verifiable ( Zeng et al., 2026a ) . Scaling long-horizon environments for training is even more difficult because rewards are sparse and available only upon task completion, depriving long-tail tasks of useful training signals. To address both limitations, we introduce a latent-world-first synthesis approach that begins by constructing a latent world , a complete and correct hidden specification of the task domain.
We first represent the underlying workflow as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) within a latent world and then progressively render the input files from that world. This procedure allows us to control task complexity while retaining every correct intermediate state, which provides a natural metric for measuring progress and therefore a verifiable dense reward for our training. Unlike pipelines that ask a language model to generate the task, inputs, and checker without a true answer, our latent world serves as an exact answer key for reliable verification.

blocks.en:
Long-horizon tasks come with sparse rewards, arriving only at task completion and submission, which notoriously starves
training on long-tail samples ( Yu et al., 2025 ; Shen et al., 2026 ; Zeng et al., 2026a ) . Group-relative policy optimization ( Shao et al., 2024 , GRPO;) normalizes rewards within a group of G G rollouts of the same task, so under terminal-only reward, a
group in which all G G rollouts fail has zero advantage everywhere and contributes nothing to the
gradient. Mid-horizon pipelines can afford to discard such groups ( Ivison et al., 2026 ; Yu et al., 2025 ) because they are rare there; on long-horizon tasks they are most common at the start of training,
when the policy is weakest and signal is needed most. We therefore introduce progress-potential reward
shaping (PPRS) into reinforcement learning (RL), which makes training efficient and makes otherwise-intractable tasks trainable. PPRS scores the agent’s workspace after every turn t t against the

Our main contributions are summarized as follows: • We propose latent-world-first synthesis , a pipeline that constructs long-horizon agentic tasks backward from a known-correct world, giving exact verification, a
controllable difficulty ladder, and a progressive reward in the middle. • We introduce Tev-Gym , the first long-horizon agent training dataset with progressive rewards, composed of
1,170 verified long-horizon task environments across 7 domains. • We present Tev -27B , trained on Tev-Gym using PPRS, and demonstrate its superior performance on ALE-CM , the TB 3.0 and TB 4.0 subsets, and TB 2.1; the same recipe applied to GLM-5.3-Flash gives Tev -320B , which improves further.

Stage 1: world construction. Each generator is a seeded program. Given a seed and a scale
tier, it procedurally generates the latent world W W , the complete, correct state of the domain
(e.g., a retail warehouse’s customers, products, and transactions, or a distributed checkpoint’s

identities, valid joins, finite measures). The same step draws a seed-derived defect plan :
exactly which records, shards, or fields of W W will later be corrupted, and by which declared
operator.

graph (DAG) of stages with explicit dependencies, permitted parallelism, and per-stage

dependent stages, defines the task’s horizon, and its stages form the skeleton of the progress
potential in § 3 .

interface, materializing the clean input files in their target wire formats: CSV and TSV
partitions, JSON records, SQLite databases, safetensors shards, stripped binaries, or
infrastructure manifests. Rendering is a pure function of W W , and before proceeding we assert
that it round-trips, i.e., that W W is recovered exactly from the rendered files. Together with the invertible corruption of Stage 4, this makes the agent’s
workspace s 0 s_{0} fully determine W W , so the correct answer is computable from what the agent
actually sees, and the ground truth is correct by construction.

Stage 4: controlled corruption. We apply the Stage-1 defect plan to the rendered files,
injecting schema drift, duplicate and missing records, categorical drift, scrambled shard indices,
stale caches, and the like (Figure 3 shows the three operators of one
environment). The corrupted tree s 0 s_{0} is the task the agent receives, and the untouched
world W W is the ground truth. Because rendering round-trips and corruption is declared and
invertible, s 0 s_{0} fully determines W W : the correct solution is computable from what the agent
sees and is known exactly without running a solver. More generally, every component of an
environment, E = ( x , s 0 , ver W , Φ W ) , E\;=\;\bigl(x,\;s_{0},\;\operatorname{ver}_{W},\;\Phi_{W}\bigr), (1) is a function of the same W W : the task prompt x x , the input tree s 0 s_{0} , the strict
pass/fail verifier ver W \operatorname{ver}_{W} , which checks the agent’s output files against W W , and
the progress potential Φ W \Phi_{W} of § 3 . This single anchor prevents artifact
drift ( Ivanov and Rana, 2026 ) , where an environment, task, and verifier generated separately
each look valid on their own yet describe different problems.

Stages 5 and 6: public specification and hidden suite. We emit the public contract, the
task prompt x x (input roles, required output artifacts and their schemas, ordered requirements,
authority-precedence rules, and the permitted toolchain), which is the only description the agent
sees. Outside the agent’s view, we seal a hidden suite used at verification time: metamorphic
transforms, which are semantics-preserving rewrites that must not change the grade, and
stale-output counterfactuals, which are plausible-but-wrong states that must fail.

blocks.en:
Our main experiments ask three questions. Does RL on Tev-Gym improve open models on the long-horizon tasks it was built for, do the gains generalize to
tasks of even longer horizon, and does the model keep its general coding competence on a standard
mid-horizon benchmark (§ 4.2 )? Finally, § 4.3 ablates our latent-world-first data and the dense reward approaches, separately.

blocks.en: 4.3 Ablation Study
blocks.zh: 4.3 发育研究

blocks.en: Due to resource constraints, we conduct the ablation study in the 9B setting of § 4.1 .
blocks.zh: 由于资源有限,我们在第9B节第4.1节中进行消化研究。

blocks.en: Ablation on data curation methods. Our pipeline differs from standard LLM-synthesized corpora in two key ways: tasks are derived from a preexisting latent world and its code-compiled workflow DAG, and verifiers evaluate against this hidden ground truth rather than only agent-visible files. Table 5 shows which components each ablation retains, with GPT-5.6 (sol, xhigh) replacing the others. Public-view verifier ablates only access to hidden ground truth by asking the model to write a verifier from the agent’s view. Prompt-first , a standard self-instruct baseline, instead replaces the entire construction pipeline by generating each prompt before its inputs, verifier, and solution, leaving no latent world or DAG. The public-view variant causes 88% of sampled groups to be discarded during training. Because both variants use terminal rewards, we compare them with the Sparse row: neither improves over the base model in S@1 ( 0.24 0.24 and 0.23 0.23 vs. 0.25 0.25 ), whereas our full method leads them by 0.05 0.05 – 0.06 0.06 in S@1 and 0.05 0.05 in P@5.
blocks.zh: 关于数据校准方法的偏差. 我们的管道与标准的LLM-合成体的corpora在两种关键方式上不同:任务来源于一个事先存在的潜伏世界及其代码编译的工作流程DAG,核查者根据这个隐藏的地面真理而不是只根据代理人可见的文件来评价. 表5显示每个部分保留哪些部分,其他部分由GPT-5.6(溶液,x高)取代。 公共视野的验证者只通过要求模型从代理者的角度写一个验证者来减少获取隐藏的地面真理的机会. 即时第一,一个标准的自我指示基线,代替整个建筑管道,方法是在其投入、核查和解决方案之前产生每个提示,从而不留下潜在的世界或DAG。 公共观点的变体导致88%的抽样群体在培训期间被抛弃。 由于两种变体都使用终端奖励,我们将它们与Sparse行比较:S@1(0.24 0.24和0.23 0.23对0.25 0.25)的基数模型都没有改进,而我们的全方位方法使它们在S@1和P@5中分别领先0.05 0.05 – 0.06 0.05。

blocks.en: Ablation on dense reward. Holding Tev-Gym fixed, we compare our PPRS, which uses return-to-go G t G_{t} with γ = 1 \gamma=1 and normalizes advantages by turn index, against terminal-only sparse reward, PPRS with per-rollout normalization ( pooled norm. ), and direct additive reward using Φ ⁡ ( s t ) \Phi(s_{t}) with γ = 0 \gamma=0 ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) . Our method provides the best balance of performance and training efficiency, improving S@1 by 0.04 0.04 over sparse reward. Turn-index normalization preserves credit for later turns by avoiding comparison of their smaller returns against the whole-rollout mean, while γ = 1 \gamma=1 propagates progress back to earlier actions. In contrast, direct additive reward repeatedly rewards high-potential states without propagating credit, leading to more rollouts exhausting the context window before submission and producing longer trajectories. The advantage over sparse reward widens further at 27B, where shaped reward trains to completion but terminal-only reward produces almost entirely zero-advantage groups and fails to complete a single optimizer step.
blocks.zh: 贬低厚厚的奖励。 持有固定的Tev-Gym,我们比较了我们的PPRS,它使用回转G t G_{t}与 γ = 1\gamma=1,并通过转动指数实现优势正常化,相对于仅限终端的零星奖励,PPRS与每期推出的正常化(集合规范),直接添加奖励使用 Φ(t)\Phi(s_{t})与 γ = 0\gamma=0 (袁等,2026). 我们的方法在业绩和培训效率方面提供了最佳的平衡,将S@1改进为0.04 0.04,优于微薄的奖励。 Turn-index正常化通过避免将其较小的回报率与整个推出的平均值进行比较来保留以后转折的信用值,而γ = 1\gamma=1则将进展推广到先前的行动. 相比之下,直接添加剂奖励一再奖励高潜力国家,而不宣传信贷,导致在提交前更多地推出上下文窗口,并产生较长的轨迹。 相对于稀少的奖励的优势在27B进一步扩大,其中形状的奖励列车完成但仅限终点的奖励产生几乎完全零优势的组别,未能完成单一的优化步骤.

blocks.en: 5 Related Work
blocks.zh: 5 相关工作

blocks.en: Synthetic corpora for coding and terminal agents. Recent corpora typically mine repositories for issues and tests or use language models to generate tasks such as bug-injected repositories and reconstructed terminal sessions ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ; Yang et al., 2025a ; Ivison et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026 ) . Other work scales executable tool-use environments and their success conditions ( Cai et al., 2025 ; Fang et al., 2025 ) , although scaling helps only when difficulty is controlled ( Zhu et al., 2026b ) . In contrast, our environments contain long, multi-stage workflows across mathematics and science, machine learning, coding, and systems; are instantiated by seeded generator code rather than directly authored by a language model; and provide a dense progress signal for every task.
blocks.zh: 用于编码和终端代理的合成蝎子. 最近的公司一般是用于问题和测试的矿井储存库,或使用语言模型生成诸如被虫注入的储存库和重建终端会话等任务(Jimenez等人,2024年;Yang等人,2025年a;Ivison等人,2026年;Lin等人,2026年). 其他工作尺度为可执行工具使用环境及其成功条件(Cai等人,2025年;Fang等人,2025年),尽管在控制困难时缩放才有帮助(Zhu等人,2026年b). 相反,我们的环境包含跨越数学和科学、机器学习、编码和系统的长期、多阶段工作流程;由种子生成器代码即时化,而不是由语言模型直接编写;并为每一项任务提供密集的进展信号。

blocks.en:
Backward construction. Deriving a task from a known solution is an established family:
denoising, controlled error injection, code mutation, environment rewinding, instruction
back-translation, and procedural puzzle generation all corrupt or invert a single artifact whose
ground truth is already
known ( Lewis et al., 2020 ; Arocena et al., 2015 ; Tran et al., 2013 ; Yang et al., 2025a ; Hariharan et al., 2025 ; Lin et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Stojanovski et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025a ; Liu et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025 ) .
We instead corrupt a rendering of an entire latent world, so the task, verifier, and progress
signal are all functions of that one world rather than separately generated factors that can drift
apart ( Zeng et al., 2026a ; Ivanov and Rana, 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:

消除、控制错误注入、代码突变、环境倒转、指令

blocks.en:
Sparse reward and dense signal in agentic RL. Existing methods avoid uninformative rollout groups by filtering identical rewards, selecting tasks near the policy’s current ability, or adding expert prefixes ( Yu et al., 2025 ; Florensa et al., 2018 ; Zhang et al., 2025c ) .
Other approaches provide denser feedback through learned judges ( Cui et al., 2025 ; Choudhury, 2025 ) or proxy signals such as test-pass rates ( Du et al., 2025 ; Shen et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) , but these require additional models or capture only terminal outcomes.
Our potential Φ \Phi instead measures exact progress and regression against the latent world at every workflow stage, without requiring a critic or language-model judge.
For full related work, please refer to Appendix D .

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We introduce a latent-world-first approach for scaling verifiable long-horizon agent training. Each task is built backward from a known-correct latent world, which is rendered into interrelated files, modified through controlled corruptions, and reused for exact verification and dense progress rewards. We instantiate this approach in Tev-Gym , a collection of 1,170 verified environments across seven domains, and show that training improves both 9B and 27B open models on ALE-CM, with gains transferring to Terminal-Bench tasks of different horizons and to a 320B base model.
One limitation of our current study is its focus on synthetic terminal environments, and the hardest benchmarks still show a gap between our models and leading frontier agents. Supporting new workflows also requires authoring and validating additional environment components. Future work could simplify this process, expand domain coverage, and combine the resulting data with stronger open models, making more professional workflows available for reproducible RL without human step labels or language-model judges.

blocks.en: Ethics statement

blocks.en:
Tev-Gym is fully synthetic: every environment is generated procedurally from a seed, contains no
data collected from people, and involves no human subjects, so the corpus encodes no private records
or proprietary code. Task specifications are drawn from public benchmarks and reference material
(Appendix A.1 ), but every artifact an agent sees is generated by the environment
itself, and third-party benchmarks and corpora used for evaluation and comparison are used under
their published licenses (Appendix A.8 ). The environments simulate
professional workflows such as data reconciliation, checkpoint consolidation, systems
administration, and the analysis of synthetic binaries and packet captures in the style of
capture-the-flag exercises. Each declares its toolchain in its public contract, the agent’s
workspace is seeded only with its public tree, and no task targets real software, systems, or people. Improving open-weight agents on
long-horizon terminal tasks carries the general dual-use considerations of more capable coding
agents; our security-flavored tasks are analysis and forensics exercises over synthetic artifacts,
the same class of task already present in public terminal-agent benchmarks. Because part of the
training mix is built against the interfaces of ALE-CM , we measure train/evaluation overlap for
every evaluation set and report it with its calibration (§ 4.1 ;
Appendix A.9 ). Frontier baselines run in their native agent harnesses,
the setting most favorable to them (Appendix C.2 ), and we discuss the limitations of
our results in § 6 .

blocks.en: A.2 Determinism, Reproducibility, and Generation Cost

blocks.en:
Every stage of § 2.1 is a pure, seeded function, and no language model

the authors (see AI use statement); running it is model-free. An environment is therefore fully
reproducible from its generator, seed, and scale tier, and two seeds of the same generator yield
provably distinct worlds (the six-seed diversity gate of Appendix A.6 ). The cost

compute: producing one environment, including running both reference solvers, sealing the hidden
suite, and previewing the progress potential Φ W \Phi_{W} , takes a median of 30 s of CPU time (90th
percentile 82 s) and no model calls, against hours of expert time per hand-authored task. Each
environment declares its toolchain (e.g., python3 , sqlite3 ) in its public
contract, and the agent’s workspace is seeded only with its public tree.

blocks.en:
Every environment is labeled on 19 axes, the required axes of the corpus coverage policy:
curriculum layer, subdomain, generator revision, scale tier, the four horizon axes (semantic, action,
operational, verification), workflow stage, tool capability, artifact role, relation type,
corruption class, source kind, license class, reward component, observed reward band, outcome
category, and failure category. The corpus must satisfy a strength-2 covering array over these
axes: for any two axes, every valid pair of their values co-occurs in at least one admitted
environment. Coverage is
extended greedily by choosing the generator, seed, and scale tier that fill the largest number of
currently uncovered pairs, so “diverse” is a checkable property of the corpus rather than a
claim. Pairwise coverage is what separates enforced from nominal diversity and rules out template locking ( Zeng et al., 2026a ) : a corpus can be balanced on every axis taken alone
while its axis values only ever appear in a few fixed combinations; a strength-2 covering array
rules this out for every pair of axes. Coverage is checked on admitted environments only, after the
gates of Appendix A.6 . Appendix A.7 reports the resulting balance
across domains and capability categories.

blocks.en: A.4 Scale Ladder
blocks.zh: A.4 升降机

blocks.en:
Each generator exposes a scale axis that tunes the size of the world. For the warehouse
environment the tiers run from 30 customers and 48 transactions per month (small) to 480 customers
and 960 transactions per month (large), with proportional growth in duplicates and missing values;
for the checkpoint-consolidation environment the ladder is the shard count crossed with the
parallelism topology (pure tensor parallelism up to combined tensor-, pipeline-, and
expert-parallel layouts). Because tasks are defined over the workflow DAG, typically five to six
critical stages with cross-stage dependencies, the action, operational, and verification horizons
grow with the tier as first-class, controllable quantities. We sample across the ladder so that the
corpus is neither uniformly trivial nor uniformly unsolvable. For the generators instantiated at all
three scale tiers, the median input tree grows from 17 files and 51 KB (unit) to 20 files and
168 KB (small) and 28 files and 586 KB (full) while the workflow DAG is unchanged.

estimated. The fixed evaluator of the difficulty protocol below, Gemini 3.6 Flash, is run on a fixed
100-task subsample of each corpus, and for every rollout we record the wall-clock time from the
agent’s first action to its last step. The interval includes every model call and retry and every
command execution in between; it excludes only sandbox setup before the first action and the
separate test run after the last step ( Tev-Gym ’s host-side grade at submission, 0.3 s at the
median, falls inside the last step). The table reports the median and mean over rollouts, in
minutes. For the prior corpora these are the rollouts of the difficulty measurement below (Harbor terminus-2 , 60 turns, 8 rollouts per task, timed by Harbor’s agent_execution interval). That budget ends only 1–13% of their rollouts, and every rollout it ends has already
run longer than its corpus’s median, so the reported prior-corpus medians equal those of an unlimited

calls), so for Tev-Gym we lift the budget until it no longer binds: we draw a fixed
100-environment subsample from all 1,170 environments (seed 20260915 , stratified by
domain 9.1–9.7) and run the evaluator in the single- bash harness of § 4.1 with a budget of 300 tool calls and 2 h of agent wall-clock per rollout, 2 rollouts per

corpora. The measure compares corpora under one evaluator and is not an estimate of

blocks.en:
Ground truth. The latent world W W is the company’s true two-period statements: 16 integer
line items in USD millions for fiscal years 2025 and 2024, each ending December 31. W W satisfies
the three identities the prompt asks the agent to verify, assets = = liabilities + + equity, net
income = = revenue − - cost of revenue − - operating expenses, and ending cash = = beginning cash + + operating + + investing + + financing cash flow, as well as the ties that connect real statements:
the four asset lines sum to total assets (FY2025: 246 + 147 + 62 + 732 = 1,187 246+147+62+732=1{,}187 ), balance-sheet cash
equals cash-flow ending cash in each year (246 and 256), and FY2025 beginning cash equals FY2024
ending cash (256). Rendering projects W W into the two public formats: each value becomes a
whole-dollar structured fact under its us-gaap concept in companyfacts.json and an
inline-XBRL row, in millions and with a stable fragment id, in the fiscal year’s 10-K. The defect
plan then corrupts the clean packet, but only in sources that the policy rejects. The original
FY2025 10-K misstates three balance-sheet lines, in its rows and in its structured facts alike (cash
239, accounts receivable 138, other current assets 726, against 246, 147, and 732 in W W ); a 10-K/A
restates one row (cash, 239 → \to 243), and the restated value is still wrong; the whole FY2025 fact
set is refiled in companyfacts.json under the 10-K/A accession with the true values, so the
structured feed and the amendment disagree about the same restatement; an 8-K reports the same
concepts under quarterly Q32025 contexts; the filings carry an “unaudited supplemental
data” section; outflows are printed in accounting parentheses, (110) ; and each line item
admits a second, company-extension concept ( jrh: ) that this seed leaves unused. Because
the defect plan is declared, the correct resolution of each of these is known without running a
solver, and the three reference deliverables follow from W W , the defect plan, and the policy
text. Since every defect lies in a rejected source, the values the policy selects are those of W W ,
and financial_statements.json is W W itself. The rejected values are also the ones that
break the ties: the original 10-K’s asset lines sum to 1,165 against its total assets of 1,187, and
neither 239 nor 243 matches the ending cash of 246. exceptions.json lists exactly the four
conflicts the defect plan created, each with the resolution the policy dictates; the amendment
entry records the filing-level choice (the 10-K/A row, 243, supersedes the original, 239), while
its selected value is the structured 246 that overrides both. evidence.csv holds one row
per line item and period, 32 in all, whose locator is the JSON pointer of the latest annual fact
and whose authority basis names the rule that selected it. A round-trip self-check reselects every
value from the public packet, verifies the three identities and the three ties above in every
period, and asserts that the observed exception set equals the expected one before the environment
is published. The grader compares the agent’s three files with these references leaf by leaf and
cell by cell at zero tolerance.

Relation to policy-invariant shaping. PPRS (Eq. ( 4 )) is not policy-invariant
shaping in the sense of Ng et al. (1999) . Classical shaping zeroes the potential of the terminal
state, so the shaping terms sum to the same constant − Φ ⁡ ( s 0 ) = 0 -\Phi(s_{0})=0 on every trajectory and leave the
objective unchanged. We keep the terminal potential, so the shaped return is terminal success plus λ ​ Φ ​ ( s T ) \lambda\,\Phi(s_{T}) and defines a graded objective; zeroing it would give every all-fail group
identical rewards again and reinstate the starvation of § 3.1 , which is why the
term is kept. What is preserved is the ranking of trajectories: a passing trajectory earns 1 + λ 1+\lambda and a failing one at most λ \lambda , so a deterministic policy that maximizes one objective maximizes

Relation to potential-based shaping. In the language of potential-based
shaping ( Ng et al., 1999 ) , Φ \Phi is the potential and r t r_{t} its difference. Classical shaping
requires that the shaped objective have the same optimal policies as the original; we deliberately
do not, because the whole point is that the shaped objective is not indifferent to partial
progress. What we retain is agreement on maximizers (any passing rollout outscores any failing one)
and anchoring ( Φ = 1 \Phi=1 exactly when the verifier passes), so the acceptance set of a task is
unchanged. This is the opposite route from the usual remedy for tasks beyond a learner’s frontier,
which is to simplify, scaffold, or defer the task until some rollout
succeeds ( Florensa et al., 2018 ; Chen et al., 2025b ; Wolf et al., 2026 ; Zeng et al., 2026a ) ; we leave
the task and the harness fixed and raise the resolution of the reward. We prefer a task-aligned
potential to the test-pass fraction of Shen et al. (2026) and the passing-assertion count of Yang et al. (2026) , which score
only what the terminal tests probe and carry no notion of regression. The signal is also denser within a group that contains a success: the lone passing rollout is contrasted not with an
undifferentiated mass of failures but with a graded spectrum of near-misses. Because Φ \Phi is
produced by a scorer with a code closure disjoint from the verifier’s and has passed the causality
and exploit-resistance gates of Appendix A.6 , none of the probed gaming strategies
applied to the public tree earns Φ > 0 \Phi>0 , and Φ \Phi rises only when the output tree matches more
of the workflow’s correct intermediate and final artifacts.

Synthetic corpora for coding and terminal agents. The first wave of agent training data
mined real repositories: SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) and SWE-Gym ( Pan et al., 2025 ) collect GitHub issues with their tests, and SWE-rebench ( Badertdinov et al., 2025 ) and
Skywork-SWE ( Zeng et al., 2025 ) automate the mining. The second wave synthesizes tasks:
SWE-smith ( Yang et al., 2025a ) injects bugs into working repositories,
SWE-Flow ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) strips a repository along its runtime dependency graph, and
R2E-Gym ( Jain et al., 2025 ) back-translates problem statements from commits. Terminal corpora
follow the same pattern at larger scale, either with a language model writing tasks, containers,
and tests that are then filtered for solvability, as in Endless
Terminals ( Gandhi et al., 2026 ) , SETA ( Shen et al., 2026 ) , and recursive solution
extension ( Li et al., 2026a ) (TMAX ( Ivison et al., 2026 ) skips this filter and lets RL drop unsolved tasks), or by reconstructing environments from agent trajectories, as in
CLI-Gym ( Lin et al., 2026 ) and Terminal-Universe ( Wu et al., 2026 ) . All of these
scale the number of instances : each instance is pull-request-sized or a single session, its
verifier is a test suite that caps the complexity a task can have, and generation depends on a
model whose output must be validated after the fact. We scale environments : a coding agent writes each generator once, the authors review
it, and instantiating it involves no model; verification is against the latent world rather than
a test suite. Closer in
spirit is the programmatic synthesis of executable, stateful tool environments,
AutoForge ( Cai et al., 2025 ) , EnvScaler ( Song et al., 2026 ) ,
ScaleEnv ( Tu et al., 2026 ) , Agent-World ( Dong et al., 2026 ) ,
EnvFactory ( Xu et al., 2026 ) , and LOGIGEN ( Zeng et al., 2026b ) , which also treats the
environment as the unit of scale ( Fang et al., 2025 ) ; these are API worlds for short
tool-use episodes, and only LOGIGEN emits a progress signal, a per-turn reward from the database’s proximity to its target state. Two findings from that line carry over: more environments alone do not help
without difficulty control ( Zhu et al., 2026b ) , and coverage rather than count is what
drives transfer ( Chen et al., 2026a ; Chen et al., 2026b ; Xu et al., 2026 ) . Our environments
differ from this family on the two properties it largely lacks: each spans a long, multi-stage workflow
across math and science, ML, and coding and systems domains rather than a short tool-use episode,
and every one ships the progress potential Φ W \Phi_{W} of § 3 rather than a bare success
condition, so the difficulty control and dense signal these two findings call for come from the
same generator that supplies coverage.

blocks.en:
Backward construction. Latent-world-first synthesis belongs to a long line of methods that
derive a task from its solution. Denoising objectives corrupt text and learn to restore
it ( Lewis et al., 2020 ) ; the data-cleaning community injects errors of controlled repairability
into clean databases to evaluate repair algorithms ( Arocena et al., 2015 ) and corrupts synthetic
person records to benchmark record linkage ( Tran et al., 2013 ) ; mutation and bug injection corrupt
working code ( Yang et al., 2025a ; Hariharan et al., 2025 ) ; CLI-Gym rewinds a healthy
environment to an earlier broken state ( Lin et al., 2026 ) ; instruction back-translation derives
prompts from answers ( Li et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) ; and procedural generators
with rule-based verifiers supply unlimited single-turn reasoning problems whose answers are known by
construction ( Stojanovski et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025a ; Liu et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025 ) .
In every case the corrupted object is a single artifact graded by a pre-existing oracle, or a
one-step puzzle. We corrupt a rendering of an entire world into many mutually constraining files of
different formats, and the oracle is the world itself; this is what lets exactness, and the ground
truth of every intermediate stage, survive a multi-hour horizon. In the taxonomy of Zeng et al. (2026a) , generation pipelines anchor on the environment, the task, the trajectory, or a
blueprint that coordinates them; anchoring on the verified terminal state itself is what removes
the artifact drift among task, environment, and verifier that separately generated factors
invite ( Ivanov and Rana, 2026 ) . Concretely, we anchor one level earlier than any object in that
taxonomy: the latent world W W itself, so that the task x x , the input tree s 0 s_{0} , the strict
verifier ver W \operatorname{ver}_{W} , and the progress potential Φ W \Phi_{W} (Eq. ( 1 )) are four
views of one object rather than four artifacts a blueprint must keep synchronized after the fact.
CLI-Gym is the closest of these in mechanism, but it rewinds a single running environment to an
earlier state and stops at one pass/fail check, with no signal over the stages in between.

blocks.en:
World-state verification, environment scaling, and long-horizon benchmarks. Verifying an
agent against the final state of a simulated world rather than against its transcript is
established in AppWorld ( Trivedi et al., 2024 ) , τ \tau -bench ( Yao et al., 2025 ) , WebArena ( Zhou et al., 2024a ) , and
OSWorld ( Xie et al., 2024 ) , all with hand-authored tasks for evaluation. Recent work generates
the world too: AgentMercury ( Jeong and Yoon, 2026 ) has a model author persistent business
worlds with executable invariants, and Zhang et al. (2026) derive dense rewards from
progress predicates over generated web sites; neither uses a declared corruption, and both depend
on a model to write the world. A growing literature argues that environments are the bottleneck of
agentic RL ( Xi et al., 2025 ; Fang et al., 2025 ; Song et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2025a ; Gandhi et al., 2026 ) ,
with the caveat that more environments alone do not help without difficulty
control ( Zhu et al., 2026b ) . Our thesis is narrower: the environments worth scaling are
those whose latent world supplies both the oracle and the progress signal. Long-horizon benchmarks
with partial credit, TheAgentCompany ( Xu et al., 2024 ) , Long-Horizon
Terminal-Bench ( Li et al., 2026b ) , PaperBench ( Starace et al., 2025 ) ,
MLE-bench ( Chan et al., 2025 ) , and ALE-Bench ( Imajuku et al., 2025 ) , target the regime we
train for, but their checkpoints are written per task by hand or graded by a model, and at tens of
instances they are evaluation sets.

blocks.en:
Sparse reward and dense signal in agentic RL. Group-relative methods discard rollout
groups with identical rewards ( Yu et al., 2025 ; He et al., 2025 ; Ivison et al., 2026 ) , schedule prompts
by difficulty ( Yang et al., 2025b ; Sha et al., 2026 ) , or seed groups with expert
prefixes ( Zhang et al., 2025c ) ; all assume enough solvable prompts to fill a batch. A
complementary line moves the tasks rather than the reward, generating or selecting them near the
learner’s current success
band ( Florensa et al., 2018 ; Guo et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025b ; Wolf et al., 2026 ) ; this keeps
groups informative but caps difficulty at what the current policy can sometimes finish. Denser
signals come from learned or judged step
rewards ( Cui et al., 2025 ; Choudhury, 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2024b ; Gunjal et al., 2025 ) ,
from advantages over recurring states ( Feng et al., 2025 ) , or from exact but proxy quantities:
similarity to an oracle patch ( Wei et al., 2025 ) , the fraction of tests
passed ( Du et al., 2025 ; Shen et al., 2026 ) , the count of passing assertions ( Yang et al., 2026 ) ,
compiler diagnostics ( Zhang and Lanser Contributors, 2025 ) , path-centric credit for evidence
gathering ( Xia et al., 2026 ) , or symbolic oracles in closed
domains ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) . Test-fraction rewards are the closest to ours and are what lets SETA
and T1 train on terminal tasks, but they score only what the terminal tests probe, are not monotone
in workflow progress, and carry no notion of regression. Our potential is exact progress against the
latent world at every workflow stage, anchored so that Φ = 1 \Phi=1 exactly when the verifier passes,
and free for every seed. A recent finding shapes how such a signal should be used: a shaping term that is not aligned
with the task collapses GRPO agents, because in all-fail groups it becomes the whole
objective ( Wang, 2026 ) . Unlike the learned or judged step rewards above, Φ \Phi needs
no trained critic or LM judge; its relation to classical potential-based
shaping ( Ng et al., 1999 ) is discussed in Appendix B .
